STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple on a white plate, photographed from directly overhead (top-down).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish white dish about 26 cm across at its widest, so its area is roughly 26 x 26 x 0.85 ≈ 570 cm^2. In the photo the plate spans about 350 px, which gives about 13 px/cm. The apple is about 128 px wide, or roughly 9.5 cm. That seems a little large, so I will use about 8 cm, since the plate may be a bit wider than I assumed.

STEP 3 - Items: One red-yellow apple (whole, with skin).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple's footprint is π x 4² ≈ 50 cm^2, which is about 9% of the plate. Food covers about 9% of the vessel in total.

STEP 5 - Volume: For a sphere of diameter 8 cm, V = 4/3 π x 4³ ≈ 268 ml. The apple is slightly flattened and has a core cavity, so the envelope is about 250 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A whole apple has a density of about 0.8 g/ml, so 250 x 0.8 ≈ 200 g. A medium apple of 8 cm is typically 180–200 g, so I use about 190 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple is about 52 kcal/100 g, so 190 g gives about 99 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium apple at roughly 190 g and 100 kcal is plausible, and nothing else is on the plate.
